title: Two Marked Notes on an Unnumbered Print Line

illustrates.quote: Treat multiple-marked or unmarked reference points on the same line as separate references. (See Sample 16-4: Two Marked Notes on an Unnumbered Print Line on page 16-21.)

blocks.text: Hath in the skirts of Norway here and there Shark'd up[ref:°] a list of lawless resolutes,[ref:°] For food and diet,[ref:°] to some enterprise That hath a stomach in't; which is no other …
blocks.features: Play-script passage, unnumbered in print; three hollow-dot reference marks after 'up', 'resolutes,', and 'diet,' on two different lines.

blocks.text:
Shark'd up: Got together in haphazard fashion; resolutes: Desperadoes.
food and diet: No pay but their keep.
blocks.features: Two bold-keyed glossary notes below a short rule; the first note bundles two of the three marked terms ('Shark'd up' and 'resolutes') together on one note line.

notes.text: Shark'd up: Got together in haphazard fashion.
food and diet: No pay but their keep.

print.surroundingText: Cross-referenced from rule 16.7.1 (via Example 16-10), illustrating two separately marked reference points ('Shark'd up' and 'resolutes') falling on the very same unnumbered print line, each still treated as its own reference.
print.printFeatures: Boxed screenshot of an unnumbered play-script passage with three hollow-dot marks and an ellipsis line, then two glossary notes below a rule.

braille.notes: Line-number field width 5 (max line number 13, two digits, +3). The two marked terms on the same braille line ('Shark'd up' and 'resolutes') each carry their own hollow-dot mark (;9"0) as separate reference points, per rule 16.7.1.

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.7.1 per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: lines 12988 and 12999 (field width 5, digits(13)+3) are each exactly 40 characters, the first right-justified to '#,-', the second a dashed page-change rule ending '#bii'. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
